g.text: GRANULE DEMO: Multi-VM Pods & Ephemeral MicroVM Containers in K8s
running inside a SINGLE Kubernetes Pod with sub-second ephemeral containers.
NAME STATUS ROLES AGE VERSION INTERNAL-IP EXTERNAL-IP OS-IMAGE
granule-demo-control-plane Ready control-plane 2m50s v1.36.1 172.31.0.2 <none> Debian GNU
--- Step 2: Provisioning Multi-VM Base Pod (web + builder) ---
NAME READY STATUS RESTARTS AGE IP NODE NOMINATED NODE
--- Step 3: Inspecting Regular VM Containers (web & builder) ---
kubectl exec granule-multi-vm -c web -- granule exec -- uname -a
Linux debuerreotype 6.16.9+ #3 SMP Fri May 8 13:58:25 UTC 2026 x86_64 GNU/Linux
kubectl exec granule-multi-vm -c builder -- granule exec -- uname -a
--- Step 4: Injecting Ephemeral MicroVM Containers into Running Pod ---
kubectl exec granule-multi-vm -c vm-ephemeral-1 -- granule ready -timeout 10s
kubectl exec granule-multi-vm -c vm-ephemeral-1 -- granule exec -- echo 'Hello World from vm-ephemeral-1!'
kubectl exec granule-multi-vm -c vm-ephemeral-2 -- granule ready -timeout 10s
kubectl exec granule-multi-vm -c vm-ephemeral-2 -- granule exec -- echo 'Hello World from vm-ephemeral-2!'
kubectl exec granule-multi-vm -c vm-ephemeral-3 -- granule ready -timeout 10s
kubectl exec granule-multi-vm -c vm-ephemeral-3 -- granule exec -- echo 'Hello World from vm-ephemeral-3!'
--- Step 5: Verifying Hardware Isolation Across All 5 VMs in Pod ---
Unique Linux Kernel Boot IDs across all Pod VM containers:
| Phase / Metric | Cold Boot | Snapshot Resume | Speedup |
| Guest VM Ready (granule ready via vsock) | 37.48s | 3.38s | 11.1x |
Demo completed successfully! All assets verified and recorded.
